_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Laos covering Austroasiatic/Tai migrations, Lan Xang kingdom (1353-1707, million elephants), split into three kingdoms, Siamese suzerainty, French Indochina 1893, Japanese occupation, independence 1953, civil war/Secret War (US bombing 1964-1973, most bombed country per capita), Pathet Lao victory 1975, communist single-party state, Mekong development, and gradual economic opening.

religion.note: Theravada Buddhism intertwined with phi (spirit) worship; that luang stupa national symbol; monks prominent in daily life; animism strong among highland minorities

ethnic_groups.name: Lao Loum (lowland Lao)
ethnic_groups.notes: Tai-Kadai; dominant politically and culturally; wet-rice farming; Buddhist; Mekong valley; speak Lao; ruling elite

ethnic_groups.name: Lao Theung (midland/Mon-Khmer)
ethnic_groups.notes: Austroasiatic peoples (Khmu, Lamet, Bit); 'original' inhabitants before Tai migration; upland swidden farming; historically marginalised ('kha'/slave pejorative); Khmu are largest single ethnic group

ethnic_groups.name: Lao Soung (highland)
ethnic_groups.notes: Hmong-Mien, Tibeto-Burman; Hmong largest subgroup (~8%); fought as CIA-backed guerrillas in Secret War; post-1975 persecution; many fled to Thailand/USA; opium cultivation historically

ethnic_groups.name: Hmong
ethnic_groups.notes: Sino-Tibetan; highland; strong identity; Secret War legacy (General Vang Pao/CIA); diaspora in USA (~300,000); some insurgent holdouts persisted decades; weaving/silverwork; animist-Christian

ethnic_groups.name: Vietnamese
ethnic_groups.notes: Urban areas; merchants; colonial-era settlers; close Lao-Vietnamese communist ties

ethnic_groups.name: Chinese
ethnic_groups.notes: Growing presence; SEZ investment; Boten-Vientiane railway (2021); Hokkien/Teochew merchants; new PRC investment migration

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Thai Dam, Iu Mien, Akha, Lahu, Tai Lue)
ethnic_groups.notes: Government recognises 50 official ethnic groups in 4 linguistic families; great ethnolinguistic diversity for small country

country_profile.notes_unique: Most bombed country per capita in history (270M cluster bombs dropped by US 1964-73, ~80M unexploded); only landlocked country in Southeast Asia; Laos-China Railway (2021); Plain of Jars (UNESCO); hydropower 'Battery of SE Asia'; UXO clearance ongoing; single-party LPRP since 1975

current_leader.name: Thongloun Sisoulith
current_leader.title: President & LPRP General Secretary
current_leader.notes: Lao People's Revolutionary Party; former PM; anti-corruption campaign; economic crisis (kip collapse, debt to China); single-party Marxist-Leninist state

prime_minister.name: Sonexay Siphandone
prime_minister.title: Prime Minister
prime_minister.notes: Son of former president Khamtai Siphandone; dynastic succession pattern common

former_leaders.name: Bounnhang Vorachith
former_leaders.notes: President & Party Secretary; conservative; maintained one-party rule

former_leaders.name: Khamtai Siphandone
former_leaders.notes: President; Pathet Lao veteran; authoritarian consolidation

former_leaders.name: Kaysone Phomvihane
former_leaders.notes: Founding leader of Lao PDR; PM then President; Vietnamese-Lao father; architect of communist state; economic reforms (NEM 1986); died in office

former_leaders.name: Souphanouvong
former_leaders.notes: 'Red Prince'; ceremonial president; Pathet Lao founder; royal family member who joined communists

910.name: Prehistoric Laos and Early Settlements
910.description: The earliest human habitation in the Mekong valley, the Plain of Jars megalithic culture, Tai migrations, and the emergence of early Austroasiatic and Tai-speaking communities.

sub_clusters.name: Prehistoric Sites and Plain of Jars
sub_clusters.description: Cave sites in Luang Prabang province, the enigmatic Plain of Jars megalithic site with its massive stone urns, and early evidence of agricultural communities in the Mekong basin.
key_events: Megalithic stone jars of the Plain of Jars created for unknown funerary or storage purposes (c. 500 BC – 500 AD)

sub_clusters.name: Early Mon-Khmer and Tai Peoples
sub_clusters.description: The Austroasiatic-speaking peoples as the original inhabitants, early Indian cultural influences via Funan and Chenla, and the beginnings of the Tai southward migration from southern China.

920.name: Tai Migrations and Muang Polities
920.description: The gradual Tai migration into the middle Mekong region, the formation of muang principalities, Khmer suzerainty, and the political fragmentation preceding the unification of Lan Xang.

sub_clusters.name: Tai Settlement and Khmer Influence
sub_clusters.description: Tai-speaking peoples migrating from Yunnan into the Mekong valley, the formation of small muang principalities, the influence of the Angkorian Khmer Empire, and the adoption of Theravada Buddhism.

sub_clusters.name: Muang Consolidation
sub_clusters.description: The proliferation of Tai muang principalities along the Mekong — Muang Sua (Luang Prabang), Muang Phuan, and others — and the political conditions leading to Fa Ngum's unification.

930.name: Kingdom of Lan Xang
930.description: The 'Kingdom of a Million Elephants' founded by Fa Ngum, the golden age under Setthathirath, the construction of That Luang and Wat Phra Kaew, and the kingdom's eventual fragmentation.

sub_clusters.name: Fa Ngum and the Founding of Lan Xang
sub_clusters.description: Fa Ngum's Khmer-backed conquest and unification of the Lao muang, the introduction of Theravada Buddhism and the Phra Bang Buddha image, and the establishment of Luang Prabang as capital.
key_events: Fa Ngum unifies the Lao muang and founds the Kingdom of Lan Xang (1353)
The Phra Bang Buddha image brought from the Khmer court to Luang Prabang (c. 1359)

sub_clusters.name: Golden Age of Setthathirath
sub_clusters.description: King Setthathirath's relocation of the capital to Vientiane, the construction of That Luang stupa and Wat Phra Kaew, the defense against Burmese invasion, and the pinnacle of Lao Buddhist civilization.
key_events: Setthathirath builds That Luang in Vientiane, the most important Lao national monument (1566)
Setthathirath successfully defends against Burmese invasion but disappears during a campaign (1571)

sub_clusters.name: Souligna Vongsa and Fragmentation
sub_clusters.description: The long peaceful reign of Souligna Vongsa, the first European visitors, and the succession crisis after his death that split Lan Xang into three rival kingdoms.
key_events: Death of Souligna Vongsa triggers the breakup of Lan Xang into Luang Prabang, Vientiane, and Champasak (1707)

940.name: Three Kingdoms and Siamese Domination
940.description: The fragmentation into Luang Prabang, Vientiane, and Champasak, the disastrous revolt of Chao Anouvong, the Siamese destruction of Vientiane, and the Lao kingdoms' vassalage to Bangkok.

sub_clusters.name: Rival Kingdoms and Foreign Interference
sub_clusters.description: The three rival Lao kingdoms playing between Siam, Burma, and Vietnam, the devastating wars, the depopulation of the Khorat Plateau, and the growing Siamese domination.

sub_clusters.name: Chao Anouvong Rebellion
sub_clusters.description: King Anouvong of Vientiane's revolt against Siamese suzerainty, the Siamese retaliatory invasion, the destruction and depopulation of Vientiane, and the effective end of Lao sovereignty.
key_events: Chao Anouvong's rebellion against Siam fails; Vientiane is razed and depopulated (1826–1829)

sub_clusters.name: Siamese Vassalage
sub_clusters.description: The Lao territories reduced to Siamese vassal provinces, the Haw Wars (Chinese bandit raids), French explorers along the Mekong, and the Franco-Siamese crisis that transferred Laos to France.

950.name: French Colonial Laos
950.description: French Indochina's 'backwater' — minimal colonial development, the Lao Issara independence movement, the Japanese interlude, and the path to independence within the French Union.

sub_clusters.name: French Protectorate
sub_clusters.description: The Franco-Siamese Treaty establishing French control, minimal colonial investment, the preservation of the monarchy, Vietnamese immigration, and the Japanese coup de force of 1945.
key_events: Franco-Siamese Treaty makes Laos a French protectorate (1893)
Japanese overthrow French administration; brief Lao Issara independence (1945)

sub_clusters.name: Independence Struggle
sub_clusters.description: The Lao Issara government-in-exile, the return of the French, the formation of the Pathet Lao under Prince Souphanouvong, and the achievement of independence within the French Union.
key_events: Laos achieves full independence from France (22 October 1953)

950.name: Laotian Civil War and Secret War
950.description: The three-faction civil war between royalists, neutralists, and the Pathet Lao, the CIA's Secret War, the massive US bombing campaign making Laos the most bombed country per capita in history.

sub_clusters.name: Three-Faction Struggle
sub_clusters.description: The tripartite conflict among royalist, neutralist, and Pathet Lao factions, the 1962 Geneva Accords, the three princes' failed coalition government, and the Ho Chi Minh Trail through Laos.

sub_clusters.name: US Secret War and Bombing Campaign
sub_clusters.description: The CIA's recruitment of Hmong forces under Vang Pao, the massive US aerial bombardment dropping over 2 million tons of ordnance, the devastation of the Plain of Jars, and the continuing UXO crisis.
key_events: US drops over 2 million tons of bombs on Laos — more than all bombs dropped in WWII combined (1964–1973)
Pathet Lao takes power; King Savang Vatthana abdicates (2 December 1975)

960.name: Lao People's Democratic Republic
960.description: Communist Lao PDR — collectivization, the refugee exodus, the New Economic Mechanism market reforms, Chinese and Vietnamese influence, hydropower development, and the UXO legacy.

sub_clusters.name: Communist Transformation and Isolation
sub_clusters.description: The abolition of the monarchy, collectivization, re-education camps, the exodus of 10% of the population as refugees (including the Hmong), international isolation, and the border war with Thailand.
key_events: Proclamation of the Lao People's Democratic Republic; monarchy abolished (2 December 1975)
Hmong refugee crisis — hundreds of thousands flee to Thailand

sub_clusters.name: New Economic Mechanism and Opening
sub_clusters.description: The NEM market-oriented reforms modeled on Vietnam's Doi Moi, normalization of relations with Thailand, ASEAN membership, the beginnings of hydropower development, and gradual economic growth.

sub_clusters.name: Modern Laos and Development Challenges
sub_clusters.description: The 'battery of Southeast Asia' hydropower strategy, the Lao-China Railway, massive Chinese investment and debt concerns, the Xe-Pian Xe-Namnoy dam collapse, and ongoing UXO clearance.
key_events: Xe-Pian Xe-Namnoy dam collapse kills dozens and displaces thousands (23 July 2018)
Lao-China Railway opens, connecting Vientiane to Kunming (December 2021)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
